long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Milan, Leonardo Del Vecchio spent part of his childhood at the Martinitt orphanage and entered factory work as a teenager. His apprenticeship in metalworking led him to Agordo, where he began making spectacle components and founded Luxottica in 1961. Del Vecchio moved into complete frames, then combined manufacturing with brand licensing, wholesale distribution and optical retail. Acquisitions including Ray-Ban and major retail chains turned the workshop into a global eyewear group. Luxottica's 2018 combination with Essilor made him chairman of the enlarged company.

Del Vecchio held the family's principal interests through Luxembourg holding company Delfin. At his death, its dominant asset was roughly one-third of EssilorLuxottica, alongside material stakes in banking, insurance and property companies. Those were Delfin assets; their gross market values did not equal personal cash or direct ownership of the underlying businesses. After his death, Delfin announced eight equal beneficiary interests and no named successor. He therefore died as Luxottica's founder and EssilorLuxottica's chairman, while control after death passed to a collectively owned holding structure.

uncertainties.detail: At death Del Vecchio controlled his interests through Delfin, whose principal asset was roughly one-third of EssilorLuxottica alongside listed banking, insurance and property stakes. Percentages varied slightly by reporting date, so the biographies use durable descriptions rather than a frozen portfolio table.

Delfin's stakes had substantial quoted market values, but gross holding-company assets were not equivalent to Del Vecchio's liquid personal wealth. EssilorLuxottica assets, revenue, employees and retail locations likewise belonged to the company rather than to him personally.

Delfin stated that eight beneficiaries each received a 12.5 percent interest and that Del Vecchio had not named a successor. Equal economic interests did not give any one beneficiary unilateral control of Delfin or direct personal ownership of its underlying listed stakes.

Delfin held meaningful finance and property investments, but EssilorLuxottica remained its dominant disclosed asset and Del Vecchio's active chairmanship. Manufacturing therefore best captures his principal industry at death; the secondary investments remain explicit in the biographies.

Subsequent changes in Delfin's portfolio, governance and beneficiary arrangements do not alter Del Vecchio's own final holdings or relationship. They are excluded except where needed to explain that control passed to a collectively owned structure.

No verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website met the acceptance threshold, which is unsurprising for a deceased founder. The exact Forbes profile and official company memorial are the only new social links proposed.

Politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters, sanctions, irrelevant private-family detail and all private-vessel research were excluded. None contributes to the identity, wealth classifications or biographies.
